children.text: Quick answer: LLM SEO is optimizing a website and a brand so that large language models — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot — know the business, find its pages and describe it correctly. A model learns about you in two ways: from its training data, which is fixed until the next model, and from live web search at the moment of the question. Each model searches a different index: ChatGPT its own index and Bing, Claude Brave Search, Gemini Google, Copilot Bing, Perplexity its own crawler. Most AI crawlers do not run JavaScript, so a site whose text is loaded by scripts can look empty to them. LLM SEO works on both paths: being present in the sources models learn from, and being readable and findable when they search.

LLM SEO overlaps with GEO and AEO, and many people use the three names for one thing. This guide takes the angle the others skip: the models themselves. What a model knows about you without searching, where each model goes when it does search, what its crawler can and cannot read, and what to change on your site so that each of them gets it right. It is based on crawler documentation from OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity and Google, a study of more than a billion AI-crawler requests by Vercel and MERJ, and a live test on 23 October 2026 in which I asked ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Claude the same question.
What is LLM SEO?
LLM SEO

(large language model search engine optimization) is the work of making a business visible and accurately described in answers produced by large language models. An LLM is the model behind an AI assistant: GPT behind ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, the models Perplexity and Copilot use. LLM SEO asks three questions about each of them:
Does the model know the business
without searching — from what it learned in training?
Can the model find and read the business's pages
when it searches the web at the moment of a question?
Is what the model says correct
— services, prices, locations, the people behind it?
Classic SEO asks whether a page ranks. LLM SEO asks whether a model can use what the page says, and whether what it says elsewhere about you agrees.
LLM SEO, LLMO and «LLM optimization»: three names, two meanings
LLM SEO
and
LLMO
(large language model optimization) mean the same marketing work. LLMO is common in German-speaking markets — «LLMO Agentur» alone is searched hundreds of times a month.
GEO
(generative engine optimization) and
AEO
(answer engine optimization) overlap with both. All four AI assistants I tested treated LLM SEO and GEO as overlapping or as the same thing. The differences are explained in
what is GEO
and
what is AEO
«LLM optimization»

has a second, unrelated meaning in engineering: making a model faster or cheaper to run — quantization, caching, inference tuning. Half of the search results for that phrase are about this. If that is what you were looking for, this article is not it.
How LLMs learn about your business: training data vs live search
A language model can know about a business in two ways, and they need different work.

picture.alt: Two paths into an AI answer: training data, fixed until the next model, and live web search at the moment of the question

contentBlocks.title: Two paths into an AI answer: training data, fixed until the

children.text: Training data.

Before release, a model is trained on a large snapshot of the web and other text. What it learns stays fixed until the next version. If your business was described in many sources before the training cutoff, the model may know it without searching; if it changed its name, prices or services after the cutoff, the model may repeat the old version. You cannot edit training data, only influence what future models learn by being present in the sources they are trained on: your site, but above all other sites, directories, articles and discussions.
Live search.

When a question needs current or specific information, the assistant searches the web, reads a few pages and writes the answer from them, usually with links. This path is what you influence directly: whether the engine's crawler is allowed in, whether it can read the page, and whether the page answers the question clearly.

Which path an assistant takes depends on the question and the product. In my test on 23 October 2026, two of the four assistants answered a definition question without searching at all — the answer came from what the model already knew.

Each assistant searches a different index with a different crawler. This is the most practical fact in LLM SEO, because a page can be visible to one model and invisible to another.

children.text: What the sources say, briefly:
OpenAI

documents three agents: OAI-SearchBot for ChatGPT search, GPTBot for training, and ChatGPT-User for pages a user asks ChatGPT to open. Sites that block OAI-SearchBot are not shown in ChatGPT search answers. According to a Peec AI report summarised in September 2026, ChatGPT increasingly answers from its own index — internally called Labrador — while still using Bing and other data suppliers.
Anthropic

lists Brave Search as the web search provider for Claude since March 2025, and documents three agents: ClaudeBot for training, Claude-SearchBot for search indexing, Claude-User for user requests. Blocking Claude-SearchBot «may reduce your site's visibility and accuracy in user search results», in Anthropic's own words.
Google

uses Googlebot for both Search and its AI features. The separate Google-Extended token controls whether content is used for Gemini models; Google states it does not affect inclusion or ranking in Google Search, which includes AI Overviews and AI Mode.
Perplexity

runs PerplexityBot to «surface and link websites» in its results and states that it is not used to train AI models. A second agent, Perplexity-User, fetches pages on a user's request and generally ignores robots.txt.
A robots.txt that keeps a site out of model training but visible in every assistant's search looks like this:

children.text: Whether to block training is a business decision. Blocking it keeps your text out of future models, but it also means the next model learns about you only from what others write.
AI crawlers and JavaScript: why your site can look empty to ChatGPT
In December 2024 Vercel and MERJ published an analysis of AI-crawler traffic across Vercel's network: more than a billion requests in a month. Two findings matter for almost every modern website.

picture.alt: AI crawler requests in one month on Vercel's network and whether each crawler renders JavaScript: Googlebot 4.5 billion, GPTBot 569 million, Claude 370 million, AppleBot 314 million, PerplexityBot 24.4 million

contentBlocks.title: AI crawler requests in one month on Vercel's network and whe

children.text: Most AI crawlers do not run JavaScript.

OpenAI's crawlers, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Meta's and ByteDance's crawlers and Common Crawl's CCBot all read only the HTML the server sends. ChatGPT's and Claude's crawlers do download JavaScript files — 11.5% and 23.8% of their requests — but do not execute them. Only Gemini, which uses Googlebot's infrastructure, and AppleBot render pages like a browser.
AI crawlers waste a third of their requests.
34.8% of ChatGPT's and 34.2% of Claude's fetches hit pages that returned 404, against 8.2% for Googlebot. They follow old and broken URLs far more often.
What this means in practice:
A single-page app built with React, Vue or Angular that renders its text in the browser sends the AI crawler an almost empty HTML shell. For ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity, that page has no content.
Prices, product details, reviews and FAQs loaded later by scripts are invisible to them even on a site that is otherwise server-rendered.
Redirects from old URLs matter more than they used to, because AI crawlers keep requesting them.

The check takes a minute: open the page's source (not the inspector) or fetch it without JavaScript, and look for the main text. If it is not in the HTML, the fix is server-side rendering, static generation or prerendering — in Next.js, the default when pages are built as server components. This site, for example, is built that way, so every article reaches every crawler as complete HTML.
How to optimize content for LLMs
1. Make every important page readable without JavaScript
Main text, prices, contact details and FAQs in the HTML the server sends. Check the source of your five most important pages.
2. Allow the search crawlers you want to appear in
OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Googlebot and Bingbot. Decide separately about the training crawlers.
3. Be indexed in every index the models use

Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools — which also feeds Copilot and part of ChatGPT — and a check that your key pages appear in Brave Search for Claude. Submit new and changed URLs through IndexNow, which Bing supports.
4. Write passages that survive being summarised

Models pull chunks, not pages. A section that names its question in the heading and answers it in the first sentence, with numbers and named sources, can be quoted on its own. A page whose answer is spread across five paragraphs cannot. The full method is in
what is AEO
5. Describe the business the same way everywhere

Name, services, locations, prices or price ranges, founding year, people. A model merges whatever it finds, and contradictions between your site, LinkedIn and old directories become contradictions in the answer.
6. Be present in the sources models learn from and search

Independent reviews, comparison articles, industry media, communities such as Reddit and GitHub for technical products, and directories that rank for your service. These sources feed both paths: future training data and today's live search.
7. Keep pages current and fix broken URLs
AI crawlers request old URLs constantly. Redirect what moved, return 410 for what is gone for good, keep the sitemap clean and show the date of the last update on pages with facts that change.
LLM SEO for each model: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot
ChatGPT.

Allow OAI-SearchBot. Be indexed in Bing, but do not stop there: ChatGPT increasingly answers from its own index. Its answers are personalised by the user's saved memory and earlier chats, so test it logged out or in a separate account without memory: as of October 2026, ChatGPT's temporary chat states that it may still use memory and custom instructions. In my study of 141 answers, ChatGPT cited only 1.6 sources per answer and referred to Google Maps in 23 of 47 answers to service questions, so a complete Google Business Profile matters here too. ChatGPT-only work is covered on the

page.
How ChatGPT search works step by step, and how to get pages cited in it, is in

Claude.

Its web search runs on Brave Search, so search for your key queries in Brave and see whether your pages are there. Allow Claude-SearchBot. Claude does not always search: for general questions it answers from training data, which is where long-standing, consistent mentions of your business pay off.
Gemini and Google's AI features.
They rely on Google's index, so classic Google SEO is the base. Blocking Google-Extended affects training, not visibility in Search.
Perplexity.

It searches on almost every question and cites many sources — 16.7 per answer in my study — mostly from the open web, often including the businesses' own sites. Allow PerplexityBot and make pages answer questions directly.
Copilot.

Grounded in Bing. Bing Webmaster Tools shows how often your pages are cited in Copilot and Bing's AI answers in its AI Performance report, the only first-party citation report any AI assistant provides so far.
llms.txt for SEO: what it does and what it does not

llms.txt is a proposed Markdown file at the root of a site that lists its most important pages for language models. It is often sold as «the robots.txt for AI», and it is not: it cannot allow or block anything. Google states that its Search systems do not use it, and no published study has found that it increases citations in AI answers. It can be useful for documentation sites whose users paste docs into coding assistants. For visibility in ChatGPT, Claude or Perplexity, robots.txt and readable HTML matter; llms.txt does not. Vercel reported in June 2025 that ChatGPT referred about 10% of its new sign-ups, up from 4.8% a month earlier and 1% six months before. Common LLM SEO mistakes
Blocking every AI bot «for safety».
A blanket block on GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot often catches the search crawlers too. Decide training and search separately.
Client-side rendering of key content.
The most common technical reason a good site is invisible to ChatGPT and Claude.
Checking only Google.
Claude searches Brave; ChatGPT increasingly searches its own index. A page that ranks in Google can be absent from both.
Measuring in your own account.
ChatGPT's memory and history shape its answers. A test in your own account mostly measures you.
Expecting llms.txt to do the work.
It does not affect visibility in any major assistant.
Optimising only your own site.
Models cite and learn from what others write about you. Without mentions elsewhere, there is little for them to find.

title: LLM SEO: How to Optimize Your Website for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity

children.text: Quick answer: ChatGPT SEO is optimizing a website so that ChatGPT finds its pages when it searches the web, cites them with a link and describes the business correctly. ChatGPT does not search your question as you typed it: it rewrites it into one or more shorter queries, often adding words like «best», «reviews» or the current year, and for non-English questions it often searches in English. It reads results from its own crawler, OAI-SearchBot, and from third-party search providers such as Bing, then cites only a handful of sites. To rank in ChatGPT, let OAI-SearchBot in, put the main text in the HTML the server sends, answer the query ChatGPT will actually search on your page, and be present in the lists, reviews and directories it finds for those queries.

ChatGPT has around 900 million weekly users, and when it answers with web search, it decides which few sites get a link. This guide explains how that decision is made, based on OpenAI's documentation for publishers, three studies of millions of ChatGPT search queries, my own analysis of 141 AI answers to buying questions, and a live test on 24 October 2026 in which I asked ChatGPT to recommend SEO consultants in Warsaw. If you want the business side — how to become one of the companies ChatGPT recommends — that is a separate
checklist for getting recommended by ChatGPT
. This article is about the search engine inside ChatGPT and how to get your pages cited by it.
What is ChatGPT SEO, and what it is not
ChatGPT SEO

is search engine optimization for ChatGPT: making a site findable, readable and citable for ChatGPT's web search, and making the business it describes known to ChatGPT's models. The same work is also called «SEO for ChatGPT», «ChatGPT search optimization» or «ranking in ChatGPT». It is part of the wider
LLM SEO
, applied to one assistant.
The phrase has a second meaning that has nothing to do with this:
using ChatGPT as an SEO tool

— writing meta descriptions, keyword ideas or articles with ChatGPT. Search results for «ChatGPT SEO» mix the two. This article is only about the first: how to appear in ChatGPT's answers, not how to use ChatGPT to do SEO for Google.
How ChatGPT search works: from a question to cited sources

ChatGPT does not search every time. For a general question it may answer from what its model learned in training, with no sources at all. When the question needs current, local or specific facts, or when the user switches web search on, it searches. That search runs in five steps.

picture.alt: How ChatGPT search works: the question is rewritten into fan-out queries, results come from OAI-SearchBot's index and third-party providers, ChatGPT-User opens selected pages, and the answer cites a few of them

contentBlocks.title: How ChatGPT search works: the question is rewritten into fan

children.text: Decide whether to search.
A definition question often gets no search; «best SEO consultant in Warsaw» almost always does.
Rewrite the question into fan-out queries.

ChatGPT sends on average 2.1 search queries per prompt, according to Peec AI's analysis of 5 million fan-outs in April 2026. They are shorter than the question and contain words the user did not type.
Collect results.
From OpenAI's own index, built by its crawler OAI-SearchBot, and from third-party search providers; Bing is the best known of them.
Open selected pages.
OpenAI's user agent ChatGPT-User fetches the pages ChatGPT decides to read. In a honeypot test by RESONEO, it was ChatGPT-User, not OAI-SearchBot, that fetched page content during a conversation.
Write the answer and cite a few sources.

After the default model switched to GPT-5.3 Instant in March 2026, ChatGPT cited 15 unique domains per response on average instead of 19, according to RESONEO's analysis of 27,000 responses. The default, faster model runs two or three rounds of search; the slower «Thinking» models chain five to more than ten.
OpenAI runs three crawlers, and only one of them decides whether you can appear in ChatGPT search:

children.text: One more rule from OpenAI's publisher FAQ: a page blocked in robots.txt can still appear in ChatGPT as a bare link and title, if OpenAI finds its URL elsewhere. To keep a page out completely, use a noindex meta tag — and let OAI-SearchBot crawl the page, or it cannot see the tag.
What ChatGPT adds to your query: fan-out queries

The search ChatGPT runs is not the question the user typed. Peec AI analyzed 5 million ChatGPT fan-out queries collected on 1–21 April 2026 and counted the words that appeared in the searches but not in the prompts.

picture.alt: Words ChatGPT adds to its search queries that the user did not type: best 15.33%, what 8.72%, review(s) 6.84%, 2026 5.44%, top 5.24%, comparison 4.48%, vs 4.27%, company 4.02%, service(s) 3.99%

contentBlocks.title: Words ChatGPT adds to its search queries that the user did n

children.text: «Best» is the most common addition; for advice-style questions such as «should I use X?» it appears in 24.3% of fan-outs. ChatGPT also adds brand names on its own: a question about «a CRM with the best support for syncing data» became a search for «CRM integration sync capabilities - Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics comparison».
What this means for a page:
ChatGPT searches for lists and comparisons.
«Best SEO consultant Warsaw 2026» returns ranking articles, directories and review sites. To be cited for such a query, a business has to be in those lists or publish a comparison page itself.
The current year matters.
A page titled «… in 2026» matches fan-outs that add the year; a page last updated two years ago looks stale next to it.
Brands ChatGPT already knows get searched by name.
If the model knows your competitors and not you, the fan-out compares them, and your page is not even a candidate. This is where the training path of
LLM SEO
meets the search path.
Why ChatGPT searches in English even when you ask in Polish

For questions in other languages, ChatGPT often runs part of its search in English. Peec AI analyzed more than 10 million prompts and 20 million fan-outs in February 2026, using only cases where the user's location matched the language of the prompt — for example, Polish prompts from Poland.

The consequences are concrete. In Peec AI's Polish example, a question about auction sites returned eBay while Allegro, by far the largest marketplace in Poland, was missing. German software questions returned no German companies. For a business that sells in Poland, Germany or France, the English web becomes part of its local visibility: an English version of the key pages, and mentions in English-language sources that ChatGPT trusts in your category, are not only for foreign clients. Google's AI features stay closer to the query language, so this is mostly a ChatGPT problem.
How to rank in ChatGPT search: what decides whether a page is cited
OpenAI does not publish ranking factors. What follows comes from its documentation, the studies above and my own tests.
1. Let OAI-SearchBot in, and decide about GPTBot separately

Check robots.txt, your firewall and your CDN's bot protection. A blanket block on «AI bots» often catches OAI-SearchBot, and then your site cannot appear in ChatGPT search at all. Blocking GPTBot is a separate decision about training and does not affect search.
2. Put the main content in the HTML the server sends

OpenAI's crawlers do not run JavaScript. If your services, prices or answers are loaded by scripts after the page opens, ChatGPT receives an empty page. View the page source and search for a sentence from the page: if it is not there, ChatGPT does not see it either.
3. Be indexed in Bing as well as Google

Bing is one of ChatGPT's search providers. Add your site to Bing Webmaster Tools, submit the sitemap and use IndexNow for new and changed pages. Many sites that rank in Google were never checked in Bing.
4. Answer the query ChatGPT will search, not only the one the user asks

Write down the ten questions your customers ask, then the searches ChatGPT would turn them into: «best … in [city] 2026», «… reviews», «… vs …», «… price». Make sure a page on your site answers each one in the first sentence under a heading that names it, with numbers, prices and dates where they exist. The method is described in detail in
what is AEO
5. Be in the lists, reviews and directories ChatGPT finds

Search your fan-out queries in Bing and Google yourself. The ranking articles, directories and review sites you see are the sources ChatGPT will read. Getting listed there, with the same name, services and prices as on your site, often matters more than another page on your own domain.
6. Publish facts ChatGPT can quote

In my live test, ChatGPT explained its shortlist with «publicly available service descriptions, review listings and published pricing» and quoted one provider's price list. A page that states who you serve, where, what it costs and how long it takes gives ChatGPT something to quote. «Contact us for a quote» gives it nothing.
7. Keep pages current
Show the date of the last update on pages with facts that change, and update them. Fan-outs that add «2026» favour pages that say they are current.
8. Cover the English path if you sell outside English-speaking markets
An English version of your main service pages, and presence in the English-language sources in your category, catches the part of ChatGPT's search that runs in English.

Check the page's meta robots tag

children.text: How to rank in ChatGPT for local businesses

Local questions — «a dentist in Warsaw», «a plumber near me», «an accountant for a small company in Kraków» — are where ChatGPT relies most on map and listing data. In my study of 141 AI answers to buying questions, ChatGPT referred to Google Maps in 23 of 47 answers, while Perplexity did so in 7 and Google AI Mode in 4. ChatGPT also cited the fewest sources: 1.6 per answer, against 16.7 for Perplexity. The full breakdown is in the
study of 141 AI answers
For a local business, that leads to four tasks:
A complete Google Business Profile
with the right categories, service areas, opening hours, photos and services.
Reviews
that mention the service and the place in the customer's own words: «they fixed the boiler in our flat in Mokotów» says more than five stars.
Consistent listings
on the directories that appear for «best [service] [city]» searches, with the same name, address and phone number as on your site.
A service page per city or district
you actually serve, with prices and the area in the text, not a page that swaps the city name in a template.
ChatGPT Shopping: how products get into ChatGPT now

ChatGPT shows product results with images, prices and comparisons. In September 2025 OpenAI launched Instant Checkout, which let US users buy from Etsy sellers without leaving the chat, with Shopify merchants to follow. In March 2026 it moved away from it: CNBC reported on 20 March that OpenAI was ending Instant Checkout in favour of retailers' apps, and OpenAI's update of 24 March recast shopping in ChatGPT around product discovery. Purchases are now completed on the merchant's site or in its ChatGPT app.
What gets products into ChatGPT now:
Product feeds.

Merchants share structured feeds — title, description, images, price, availability — through OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol or through platforms. Shopify merchants are included through Shopify Catalog without extra work.
Crawlable product pages.
The same OAI-SearchBot rule applies: a blocked shop does not appear in search answers.
Complete product data.

Brand, GTIN, dimensions, materials, availability and the attributes people filter by. ChatGPT may shorten titles and write its own labels such as «budget-friendly», so the facts have to be in the data.

OpenAI says product results «are not ads and are not influenced by partnerships». Reviews and comparison articles still shape which products ChatGPT puts forward, through the same fan-out searches as everything else.
Why ChatGPT answers differ between users
Two people asking ChatGPT the same question can get different businesses. There are four reasons, and they all affect how you should test.
Different models.

More than 90% of ChatGPT's weekly users are on the free plan, according to RESONEO, and the default model searches less and cites fewer sources than the paid «Thinking» models. Since 7–8 October 2026 the default is GPT-6. Test in the free plan, because that is what most of your customers see.
Memory and personalization.

ChatGPT uses saved memories, earlier chats and custom instructions. The temporary chat does not reliably remove this: on 24 October 2026 ChatGPT's temporary chat itself stated that it «may use memory, plugins and custom instructions». Test logged out or in a separate account without memory.
Location and language.
ChatGPT takes the user's approximate location into account for local questions, and the language of the question changes how much it searches in English.
Randomness.
The same question asked twice can return different sources. One check is an impression; ten checks of the same question set are a measurement.

picture.alt: ChatGPT's temporary chat, 24 October 2026 (Polish interface): «This chat may use memory, plugins and custom instructions, but it will not appear in history»

contentBlocks.title: ChatGPT's temporary chat, 24 October 2026 (Polish interface)

children.text: Ads.

OpenAI started testing ads in ChatGPT in February 2026, for logged-in adult users on the Free and Go plans, and by October 2026 had extended them to 89 countries. Ads are labelled as sponsored and shown separately from the answer, and OpenAI states that «ads do not influence the answers ChatGPT gives you». So ChatGPT SEO and ChatGPT ads are two different channels, as they are in Google.
How to track ChatGPT traffic and citations
Referrals in analytics.

ChatGPT adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to the links it shows, so in GA4 these visits appear under that source. Create a channel group for AI assistants that also covers perplexity.ai, gemini.google.com, claude.ai and copilot.microsoft.com.
The October 2026 drop that was not a drop.

After GPT-6 reached paid plans on 7 October and free plans on 8 October 2026, many links in ChatGPT's answers opened without the UTM tag or a referrer. LLM Pulse measured a fall of about 46% in ChatGPT sessions from 9 October across the sites it monitors, while Direct traffic rose by almost the same amount. Annotate 9 October 2026 in your reports and compare ChatGPT and Direct together on the pages ChatGPT used to send traffic to.
Server logs.

Filter by the user agents OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User. OAI-SearchBot shows what ChatGPT indexes; ChatGPT-User shows which pages it opened to answer real questions — the closest thing to impressions you can get.
A fixed question set.

Twenty to fifty questions your customers ask, checked monthly in the free plan, logged out. Record whether you are named, whether your site is cited with a link, whether the description is right, and which sources were cited instead. The method is described in
how to check what AI says about your company
ChatGPT does not offer site owners a report of their impressions or citations. Bing Webmaster Tools has one for Copilot and Bing's AI answers, which is worth checking for the overlap.
Live test: what ChatGPT answered about SEO consultants in Warsaw
On 24 October 2026 I asked ChatGPT, with web search on, in a temporary chat: «Who are the best SEO consultants in Warsaw for a small business?»

picture.alt: ChatGPT's answer to «Who are the best SEO consultants in Warsaw for a small business?», 24 October 2026: it compares practical experience, technical and content SEO and transparent pricing, then lists consultants «based on publicly available service descriptions, review listings and published pricing»

contentBlocks.title: ChatGPT's answer to «Who are the best SEO consultants in War

children.text: What happened:
ChatGPT named five consultants and agencies.
I do not name them here; the point is the mechanism, not the list. My own business was not among them, although I am an SEO consultant in Warsaw and my site publishes prices.
Its sources were the providers' own sites and one Polish business magazine's ranking article.
It explained its own criteria:
«publicly available service descriptions, review listings and published pricing». For one provider it quoted the price list from its website.
Its advice to the user was to compare experience, technical and content SEO, and transparent pricing
— the same things that got the named providers onto the list.

The lesson is uncomfortable and useful. Publishing prices is necessary but not enough: the named providers were also present in the source ChatGPT found for «best SEO consultants Warsaw» — a ranking article. A business that is missing from the lists ChatGPT's fan-out queries return is missing from the answer, however good its own pages are.
Common ChatGPT SEO mistakes
Blocking OAI-SearchBot by accident.
A firewall rule or a CDN's «block AI bots» switch removes a site from ChatGPT search. Check it before anything else.
Optimizing for the question instead of the search.
Users ask long questions; ChatGPT searches short queries with «best», «reviews» and the year. Pages that only match the long question miss the search.
Ignoring the English web.
For non-English markets, a large share of ChatGPT's research runs in English. A business with no English presence leaves that part to competitors.
Testing in your own account.
Memory, chat history and custom instructions shape the answer, and the temporary chat may still use them. Test logged out.
Reading the October 2026 drop as lost visibility.
Since GPT-6, many ChatGPT visits are counted as Direct. Check both channels before changing anything.
Confusing ChatGPT SEO with ChatGPT ads.
Ads are a paid placement next to the answer; they do not change what the answer says.
Waiting for a ranking report.
ChatGPT does not have a Search Console. Measuring with a fixed question set and server logs is the only way to see change.
Where to start with ChatGPT SEO

Open your robots.txt and your CDN's bot settings and make sure OAI-SearchBot is allowed. View the source of your main service page and look for its main text. Then write down five questions your customers ask, turn each into the search ChatGPT would run — «best … in [city] 2026» — and look at what Bing and Google return for it: those are the sources you need to be in. Ask ChatGPT the same five questions logged out and record who it names and which sites it cites.

If you would rather have this done for you, I offer it as a separate service: a ChatGPT visibility audit from 250 €, one-off; monthly ChatGPT SEO work from 800 €; monitoring alone from 250 € a month. What each includes is on the
ChatGPT SEO services
page, or
write to me
with your site and the questions your customers ask.

ChatGPT SEO is optimizing a website so that ChatGPT finds its pages when it searches the web, cites them with a link and describes the business correctly. It is not the same as using ChatGPT as a tool for SEO work.

items.question: What is ChatGPT SEO?

children.text: Allow OAI-SearchBot, put the main text in the server HTML, get indexed in Bing, answer the queries ChatGPT actually searches — often with «best», «reviews» and the year — and be listed in the rankings and directories it finds for them. For local businesses, add a complete Google Business Profile and reviews.

items.question: How do I rank in ChatGPT?

children.text: From OpenAI's own index, built by the OAI-SearchBot crawler, and from third-party search providers, of which Bing is the best known. Pages it decides to read are opened by the ChatGPT-User agent.

items.question: Where does ChatGPT get its search results from?

children.text: No. OpenAI shows labelled ads to Free and Go users and states that ads do not influence the answers. Product results in ChatGPT Shopping are also described by OpenAI as not ads and not influenced by partnerships.

items.question: Can I pay to rank in ChatGPT?

children.text: No. GPTBot collects data for training. ChatGPT search uses OAI-SearchBot. Blocking OAI-SearchBot is what removes your pages from search answers.

items.question: Does blocking GPTBot remove my site from ChatGPT?

children.text: Usually because they appear in the sources ChatGPT finds for its fan-out queries — rankings, directories, review sites — or because the model already knows them by name. Check which sources ChatGPT cites for your key questions, then work on being present there.

items.question: Why does ChatGPT recommend my competitors and not me?

children.text: Technical fixes show quickly: OpenAI says robots.txt changes for OAI-SearchBot take about 24 hours, and new pages appear after the next crawl. Appearing in third-party lists and reviews takes weeks to months. Becoming known to the model itself takes until the next model is trained.

items.question: How long does ChatGPT SEO take?

children.text: OpenAI names its own crawler and third-party search providers without listing them all; Bing is the one usually named. Whatever the providers, pages that rank well in classic search are the usual candidates. And in my study ChatGPT referred to Google Maps in about half of its answers to local service questions, so a Google Business Profile matters for ChatGPT too.

children.text: Quick answer: Attorney SEO is the work that makes a lawyer or law firm appear when people search for legal help — in Google's map, in the regular results, in AI answers and in legal directories. For a solo lawyer or a small firm it comes down to five things: a complete Google Business Profile for each office, one page for each legal problem you handle, attorney bio pages that show real experience, a steady flow of genuine reviews, and a website that loads fast and answers the call on a phone. All of it has to stay within your state's bar advertising rules, which shape what you can say about results, specialization and reviews.

Lawyers are told that SEO is expensive, slow and best left to an agency. Part of that is true: legal search is one of the most competitive markets online, and a click on a legal ad is among the most expensive in any industry. But most of what decides whether a small firm gets found is not secret and not technical. It is a set of decisions a lawyer can understand and check: which cases to target, how the Google profile is filled in, what each page says, how reviews are handled.

This guide goes through those decisions in the order I would make them, with the data behind each one and the bar rules that apply. It is written for solo attorneys and small law firms in the US, with notes for other countries where the rules differ. If you would rather hand the work over, the
law firm SEO service page
describes how I do it; this article is meant to be useful whether you hire anyone or not.
What attorney SEO is, and how legal SEO differs from SEO for other businesses
Attorney SEO

(also called lawyer SEO, legal SEO or SEO for law firms) is search engine optimization for legal services: making sure that a person with a legal problem finds your firm, trusts what they see and contacts you. The goal is not traffic. The goal is consultations and signed cases.
The method is the same as for any business — useful pages, a sound website, a strong local profile, mentions on other sites — but four things make the legal market different:
Google is stricter about legal content.

Google's quality guidelines treat pages that can affect a person's money, safety or rights as «Your Money or Your Life» (YMYL) topics and expect visible expertise behind them. Earlier editions named divorce, child custody and wills as examples; the current one defines YMYL by the harm a page can do, and a wrong answer about a deadline or a custody rule clearly qualifies.
Bar rules limit what you can say.

You cannot promise outcomes, call yourself a specialist without certification in most states, or pay someone to recommend you. Ordinary marketing copy («the best divorce lawyer in town») often breaks these rules.
Most clients search locally and urgently.
Someone arrested tonight or injured in a crash this morning is not reading blog posts. They see the map, a few results, and they call.
Paid search is expensive.

In LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks, attorneys and legal services pay $9.87 per click on average and $131.63 per lead. SEO does not replace ads overnight, but every client who finds you without an ad is a lead you did not pay $130 for.
How clients find a lawyer online in 2026: search, reviews and AI
Before choosing tactics, it helps to see what a potential client actually does. Several 2025–2026 studies of US legal consumers agree on the pattern.

picture.alt: How a client finds a lawyer in 2026: research online even after a referral, compare two or more firms by reviews, contact the one that answers first; AI is used for questions, rarely for hiring

contentBlocks.title: How a client finds a lawyer in 2026: research online even af

children.text: They research even when someone recommended you.

In Scorpion's survey of 3,000 US adults (September 2025), 74% researched a law firm online even after getting a referral. In Martindale-Avvo's January 2026 report, 92.4% said they were likely to research their legal issue online before contacting a lawyer.
Most start with a search engine.
In AttorneySync's 2026 study, where 320 personal injury clients were recorded while searching for a lawyer, 54.4% started with a search engine and 13% with an AI tool.
Reviews decide the shortlist.

In the Scorpion survey, 57% named online reviews as their main deciding factor, and more than half would not consider a firm rated below 4 stars. In the AttorneySync recordings, the firms people clicked had a median rating of 4.9.
They contact more than one firm, and they do not wait.
67% of the AttorneySync participants contacted two or more firms, and 40% moved on at once if they got no response. In the Scorpion survey, 72% would not wait more than 24 hours for a callback.
Many firms do not answer.
When Clio's researchers posed as potential clients and contacted 500 US firms in 2024, only 40% answered the phone and 33% replied to an email; 48% neither answered nor called back.
AI is used for questions, not yet for hiring.

Clio's 2026 Legal Trends Report (26 October 2026) found that 24% of US adults had used AI to answer a legal question, and 46% would consult AI before contacting a lawyer. But in the AttorneySync study fewer than 2% said they would use AI to choose the lawyer they hire.

What this means for SEO: being visible is only half the job. A firm that ranks well but has a 3.8 rating, or that sends calls to voicemail, loses the client it paid to attract. The plan below treats reviews and response speed as part of SEO, because for a law firm they are.
Where a law firm can appear: the map, organic results, AI Overviews and directories
«Ranking on Google» means at least four different places, and each one is won differently.

picture.alt: Two Google results pages: «divorce lawyer in Austin» shows ads, the map with three firms, then directories and firm websites; «how is child custody decided in Texas» shows an AI Overview with cited sources, then articles

contentBlocks.title: Two Google results pages: «divorce lawyer in Austin» shows a

cells: Google Business Profile, distance, reviews, relevance of the category
Practice-area pages, site quality, links and mentions
City and practice searches, specific legal problems
Clear answers on pages Google already trusts
Questions: «how is custody decided», «can I sue my employer for…»
Your profile there and the directory's own strength
Almost every legal search; also a source for AI answers

children.text: How often legal searches show an AI Overview

Legal-marketing blogs often say that AI Overviews appear on «78% of legal queries». I could not find any study behind that number. The press release that spread it credits Semrush, but Semrush's published study does not contain it. The best data I found is from Ahrefs, which analysed 146 million results pages in September 2025: AI Overviews appeared on 23.6% of legal results pages. Across all topics, they appeared on 57.9% of question-style searches and on only 7.9% of searches with local intent.

A smaller manual study by Whitespark (May 2025) shows the same split: searches like «personal injury lawyers in Phoenix» showed an AI Overview 15% of the time and a map pack 93% of the time, while informational questions in the same industries showed one 92% of the time.

The practical conclusion: the searches that bring clients ready to hire are still decided mostly by the map and the organic results. AI answers matter for the questions people ask before they are ready — and that is where they form their first impression of who knows the subject.
Attorney SEO strategy: a 90-day plan for a solo lawyer or a small law firm
A small firm cannot do everything at once, and does not need to. This is the order I would follow; each step builds on the previous one.

picture.alt: A 90-day attorney SEO plan: weeks 1–2 choose practice areas and cities, fix the Google Business Profile; weeks 3–6 practice-area pages and bios; weeks 7–10 reviews and directories; weeks 11–13 content and measurement

contentBlocks.title: A 90-day attorney SEO plan: weeks 1–2 choose practice areas

children.text: Choosing practice areas and cities to win first

The biggest mistake in attorney SEO strategy is aiming at the most expensive search in the biggest city: «personal injury lawyer Los Angeles» is fought over by firms with national budgets. A small firm wins first where competition is thinner and its experience is real:
A narrower practice
: «contested custody» rather than «family law», «truck accident» rather than «personal injury».
A smaller place
: a suburb or county seat where your office actually is, rather than the metro area.
A language
: if you serve clients in Spanish, Polish or Vietnamese, a page in that language faces a fraction of the competition.
A problem with no good answer yet
: look at the results for the questions your clients ask you. If the top results are thin directory pages, that is your opening.
Write down three to five combinations of practice and place. Everything else in this plan is built around them.
Attorney SEO keywords: what clients type before they call a lawyer

Lawyers describe their work in legal terms; clients search in their own words. A client does not search «tortious interference» — they search «my former employer is telling clients lies about me». Good attorney SEO keywords come from three sources:
Your intake notes.
The exact phrases people use when they call. These are your best keywords and no tool has them.
Google's own suggestions.
Type the start of a client's question and look at the autocomplete, the «People also ask» box and the related searches at the bottom of the page.
A keyword tool for volumes.
To compare «child custody lawyer» with «custody attorney» in your state, any keyword tool will do. Volumes for small cities are often shown as zero; that does not mean nobody searches.
Group the phrases by the problem they describe, not by the words. «DUI lawyer», «drunk driving attorney» and «arrested for DWI what to do» are one problem and belong on one page.
Google Business Profile for a law firm and for each attorney

For local searches, the Google Business Profile matters more than anything on your website. Google's guidelines contain rules written specifically for professions like law, and breaking them is the most common reason a firm's listing gets suspended or never ranks:
Name without keywords.

The profile name must be the real name of the firm, as it appears on your signage and letterhead. Google's guidelines say that adding unnecessary information to the name — service descriptions, locations — is not permitted. «Smith Law — Best Divorce Lawyer Austin» invites a suspension; «Smith Law PLLC» is correct.
One profile per office, a real office.
Google states that virtual offices are not eligible. A shared coworking desk you never use is not an office.
Profiles for individual attorneys.

Google calls lawyers «individual practitioners»: an attorney who serves clients publicly may have a profile of their own, in addition to the firm's. A solo lawyer practising under a firm brand should have one profile, named «Firm name: Attorney name». An attorney should not have several profiles for different practice areas.
Categories by practice.
Choose the most precise primary category («Divorce lawyer», «Criminal justice attorney», «Personal injury attorney») and add the others as secondary.
Everything else filled in.
Hours, phone, website link to the right office page, languages spoken, photos of the real office and people, and questions and answers that reflect what clients actually ask.

Check that the name, address and phone match exactly across the profile, your website and the directories. Inconsistent details are one of the few technical things that still confuse Google's local results.
Practice-area pages: one page per legal problem
A single «Practice areas» page listing ten services ranks for none of them. Each problem a client searches for needs its own page, and each page has to do more than say you handle it.

picture.alt: What a practice-area page needs: the problem in the client's words in the title, a short answer, how the process works in your state, costs and fees, the attorney who handles it, results with disclaimers, questions, and a call button

contentBlocks.title: What a practice-area page needs: the problem in the client's

children.text: A strong practice-area page:
Names the problem the way the client does
in the title and the first sentence: «Contested custody lawyer in Travis County», not «Family Law Services».
Answers the first question at once
: how the process works in your state, how long it usually takes, what the first consultation involves.
Explains fees honestly
: hourly, flat or contingency, and what is included. Clients compare firms on this, and it is exactly the kind of fact AI answers quote.
Shows who does the work
: the attorney's name, photo, bar admission and a link to their bio.
Includes results only with the disclaimers your state requires
(more on that below).
Ends with a clear next step
: a phone number that dials on tap and a short form.

For firms with several offices, the same logic applies to cities: one page per real office, with content that is actually about that place — the courthouse, local procedures, how to get there. Copies of one page with the city name swapped are what Google's spam policies call doorway pages; Google's own example of doorway abuse is pages «targeted at specific regions or cities that funnel users to one page».
Attorney bio pages that show experience

The bio page is where Google — and the client — checks whether real expertise stands behind the content. It should include bar admissions and years of practice, education, the courts you appear in, publications and talks, languages, memberships, and a plain description of the cases you take. A professional photo matters more than lawyers expect: in a market where everyone claims experience, a real face is one of the few things that cannot be copied.

Link each practice-area page to the attorney who handles it, and each article to the attorney who wrote or reviewed it. That connection between content and a named, licensed person is the clearest expertise signal a legal website can send.
Getting reviews, and replying to them under ABA Formal Opinion 496
Reviews influence both the map ranking and the client's decision, so they need a routine, not occasional luck:
Ask every satisfied client
, at the moment the matter ends well, with a direct link to your Google profile. A short text message works better than an email.
Never pay for reviews, write them yourself or offer anything in exchange.
Besides breaking Google's rules, a fake review is a false statement about your services, which bar rules prohibit.
Do not filter.
Asking only the clients you expect to be happy («review gating») is against Google's policies.
Replying to negative reviews is where lawyers get into trouble. The American Bar Association addressed it in
Formal Opinion 496

(January 2021): a lawyer's duty of confidentiality applies to online replies, even if the client already disclosed the information themselves, and a negative review is not a «controversy» that allows a lawyer to reveal client information in self-defense. The opinion suggests that a lawyer may not respond at all, may ask the platform to remove a review that is false, may invite the person to discuss the matter offline, or may reply with a statement such as: «Professional obligations do not allow me to respond as I would wish.»
A safe reply never confirms that the reviewer was a client and never mentions anything about a case.
Legal directories worth keeping: Avvo, Justia, FindLaw, Super Lawyers

Directories rank for a large share of legal searches and are often cited in AI answers, so a complete, consistent profile on the main ones is worth an afternoon. Two things are worth knowing before you pay for any upgrade:
Many of them have one owner.

Internet Brands owns Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Lawyers.com and Nolo, and bought FindLaw from Thomson Reuters in December 2024. A listing on four of these sites is, in practice, a relationship with one company.
Paying for a «recommendation» is restricted.

ABA Model Rule 7.2(b) prohibits giving anything of value for recommending a lawyer, with exceptions for the reasonable cost of advertising. In 2024 the New York State Bar's ethics committee (Opinion 1267) found that paying a site that presents the lawyers it lists as vetted for «excellent qualifications» counts as paying for a recommendation. A paid placement that is clearly an ad is one thing; a paid «top attorney» badge is another.

Start with the free profiles: Avvo, Justia, FindLaw, your state bar's directory, and Super Lawyers or Best Lawyers if you are selected. Make the name, address, phone and practice areas identical to your Google profile.
Attorney SEO content: answering legal questions clients ask

Content for a law firm is not a blog about firm news. It is answers to the questions clients ask before they hire anyone: «Can I move out of state with my child after a divorce in Texas?», «What happens at an arraignment?», «How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Florida?». Each good answer is a chance to rank, to be cited in an AI Overview and to show the reader that you know the subject.
Rules for legal content that ranks:
One question per article, answered in the first two sentences
, then explained in detail.
Jurisdiction-specific
: the statute, the deadline, the court — general national content is what directories already publish.
Reviewed and signed by a licensed attorney
, with the date it was last checked. Laws change, and an outdated article about a deadline can harm a reader.
Linked to the practice-area page
where the reader can act on it.
A «not legal advice» note
, short and at the end, not a wall of disclaimers before the answer.
Two good articles a month, each answering a real client question in depth, do more than daily posts written to fill a calendar.
Links and mentions a law firm can earn

Links from other websites are still one of Google's strongest signals, and for law firms the good ones come from real activity: bar association and court-related pages, law school alumni pages, local news that quotes you on a legal question, community organizations you support, podcasts and webinars you appear on, and articles you write for trade publications. Each of these is also a mention that AI systems can find.
Avoid link packages and «guest posts» bought in bulk. They are against Google's spam policies, and many of the sites that sell them are exactly the low-quality sources Google discounts.
Technical SEO for law firm websites: checks a lawyer can run
You do not need to read code to check the technical basics. Most problems on law firm websites fall into a handful of groups:
Speed on a phone.
Run your main pages through Google's PageSpeed Insights on mobile. Heavy sliders, video backgrounds and stock-photo carousels are the usual reasons for a slow site.
The phone number dials on tap
on every page, and the form works and sends a copy to an inbox someone reads.
Every important page is indexed.
In Google Search Console, check the «Pages» report; type site:yourfirm.com into Google to see what is there.
One address per page.
The site opens on one version (with or without «www», always https) and the others redirect to it.
Structured data uses current types.

On schema.org, the type «Attorney» is now marked as deprecated, with LegalService recommended instead. LocalBusiness or LegalService markup with your name, address, phone and opening hours helps search engines read the basics.
No review stars from your own reviews.
Google does not show star ratings in results for reviews that a business collects and displays about itself. Markup for them does not help.
If you want a deeper check, a
law firm SEO audit
covers the technical side together with practice-area structure and competitors.
Attorney SEO and bar advertising rules in 2026

Your website, your Google profile and your directory listings are all lawyer advertising. Every state has its own version of the rules, so check yours, but most follow the ABA Model Rules, and a few recent changes are worth knowing.

columns: What you want to do in SEO

cells: ABA Model Rule 7.1: no false or misleading communication
No promises of outcomes; results only with context, so a reader does not expect the same
Only if certified by an approved body that you name; Florida also allows objectively verifiable claims
Pay for leads or a directory listing
Paying for advertising and for leads is allowed if the provider does not recommend you or pretend to have analysed the person's problem
Put your contact details on pages
At least one responsible lawyer or firm name with contact information
Contact people who need a lawyer
No live person-to-person solicitation for money; ABA Formal Opinion 501 (2022) covers this
No client information, not even that the person was a client

children.text: State differences that affect a website:
New York

rewrote its advertising rule with effect from 1 June 2026, replacing it with a version based on the ABA rule. The New York State Bar Association's own explanation: you no longer have to put the words «Attorney Advertising» on everything. The former rule required that label on a firm's home page and specific wording on past results.
Texas

requires advertisements to be filed with the State Bar's Advertising Review Committee, but exempts information and links on a law firm website except the home page, and the home page too if its contents are otherwise exempt.
Florida

exempts the information on a lawyer's website from filing for review, requires past results to be objectively verifiable, and has detailed requirements for testimonials, including a disclaimer that the reader may not obtain the same result.
California
moved its old mandatory disclaimer for testimonials into an optional comment when it adopted the current Rule 7.1 in 2018: a disclaimer «often avoids creating unjustified expectations».

Outside the US the rules can be stricter or looser — in the UK, advertising is governed by the SRA and the BSB; in Poland, advocates were allowed to use commercial communications only in 2023 — but the principle is the same: facts, not superlatives.
This is a summary for planning SEO work, not legal advice; your state bar's ethics opinions are the final word.
Lawyer SEO in AI search: ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode (GEO, AEO)

AI search changes where the first contact happens. A person who asks ChatGPT or Google «how is child support calculated in Ohio» gets an answer with a few cited sources before they see any law firm. Being one of those sources is the work now called
GEO
(generative engine optimization) or
AEO
(answer engine optimization); I explain both in detail in
What is generative engine optimization
For a law firm, it comes down to a few concrete steps:
Answer questions directly.

AI systems quote sentences that answer a question on their own. A section that starts with «In Ohio, child support is calculated using…» is quotable; a section that starts with «Every family is different» is not.
Put facts in text
: fees, practice areas, languages, counties served, the attorney's name and bar admission. AI answers cite what is written, not what is in a PDF or an image.
Be present where AI looks.

For «best [practice] lawyer in [city]», AI answers often cite directories and lists as well as firm websites. A consistent profile on Avvo, Justia, FindLaw and your bar's directory feeds those answers.
Let AI crawlers in.
Check that your robots.txt and your hosting firewall do not block OAI-SearchBot (ChatGPT search) or Google. Some security plugins and hosting firewalls block «unknown bots» by default.
Keep the main text in the HTML
the server sends, not loaded later by JavaScript; several AI crawlers do not run JavaScript.
How ChatGPT decides which pages to cite is a subject of its own; I cover it in
ChatGPT SEO
Attorney SEO marketing vs Google Ads and Local Services Ads: cost and timing
SEO, Google Ads and Local Services Ads are not alternatives; they work on different timelines.

children.text: For legal advertisers, Local Services Ads show at the very top of the page, with your photo, rating and the «Google Verified» badge. Google has started moving Local Services Ads into Performance Max campaigns from August 2026, beginning with home services; legal categories have not been named yet.

A sensible mix for a small firm: Local Services Ads or a small search campaign for immediate calls in your main practice, and SEO for the long term, so that the cost per client falls over time instead of rising with every price increase from Google. What SEO for a law firm costs is broken down in
How much SEO for a law firm costs
How to measure attorney SEO: calls, consultations and signed cases
Rankings and traffic are signals, not results. Measure what pays the bills:
Calls from Google.
The Google Business Profile shows calls and direction requests; a call-tracking number on the website shows calls from organic search.
Form submissions
, tracked as conversions in Google Analytics and marked by source.
Consultations booked
— ask every new client how they found you, and record it in your case-management system.
Signed cases and their value
, by source, once a quarter.
Visibility for your three to five target combinations
: map position for «[practice] lawyer [city]», and whether you are cited in AI answers to your key questions (ask them logged out, or in a fresh account without memory).
If calls rise but consultations do not, the problem is intake, not SEO.

children.text: Attorney SEO mistakes that cost cases
Keywords in the Google profile name.
It may help for a few weeks, then the profile is suspended or edited by Google, and a suspension can take weeks to resolve.
City pages with nothing but a swapped city name.
These are doorway pages under Google's spam policies and drag down the rest of the site.
A virtual office to «rank» in another city.
Not eligible under Google's rules, and a misleading statement about where you practise.
Bought or self-written reviews.
A breach of Google's rules and of the bar rule against false statements.
«Specialist», «expert», «best»
without certification or an objective basis.
Paying a directory or lead service that presents itself as recommending you.
See Rule 7.2(b) and NYSBA Opinion 1267.
Replies to reviews that confirm the person was a client.
See Formal Opinion 496.
A website that nobody answers.
All the SEO in the world does not help if 48% of calls go unanswered, as in Clio's test.
One page for all practice areas.
It ranks for none of them.
What to do yourself and when to hire an attorney SEO expert

A solo lawyer can do most of the first 90 days alone: the Google profile, reviews, directories, bios and a few practice pages are a matter of decisions and an evening a week. Outside help pays off for the technical side, for building a site structure that grows without duplicate pages, for content in competitive practices, and for measuring what actually brings signed cases.
When choosing an attorney SEO company or consultant, ask:
Who exactly will do the work
, and will you speak to that person?
What will be done in the first three months
, page by page?
How do they handle your state's advertising rules
in the copy they write?
What do they measure
— rankings, or calls and consultations?
Who owns the website, the content and the Google profile
if you part ways?
Do they build links
, and from where?

Be cautious with guarantees of first place in Google, contracts that lock you in for a year before any work is shown, and offers that include the website, content and the Google profile «under the agency's account».
If you want to hand the work over, I do SEO for law firms as one consultant: an audit from 250 €, monthly work from 800 €. What each includes is on the
law firm SEO
page; for firms that live from the map there is
local SEO for lawyers
, and for the most competitive practice,
personal injury SEO
Where to start with attorney SEO

This week, open your Google Business Profile and compare its name with your letterhead; remove anything that is not your firm's real name. Write down the three practice-and-place combinations you most want to win. Search for each one on your phone and note who appears in the map, in the results and in any AI answer. Then ask your last five satisfied clients for a review.
Those four steps cost nothing and show you where you stand. If you want someone to take the next steps with you,
write to me
with your website, your main practice and the area you serve, and I will tell you what I would do first.

The first movements — fixes to the Google profile, new pages getting indexed — show in about 1.5 months. Steady growth in calls takes three to six months. In the most competitive practices, such as personal injury in a large city, it takes longer, which is why starting with a narrower practice or a smaller area makes sense.
